source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Current POSIX.1-2024 barrier and memory-synchronization rules; Java SE 26 CountDownLatch one-shot and visibility behavior, CyclicBarrier reuse, action, and all-or-none breakage, and Phaser registration/termination/tiering; and Rust 1.98 Barrier reuse and leader behavior were verified against official specifications.

evidence: Reviewed phase g, registered P, arrived A, unarrived U, latch count C, broken/terminated flags, arrival times, and generation-order notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: One-shot completion, fixed generations, dynamic membership, and abnormal termination are distinct.

evidence: Executed all 90 order-preserving two-arrival histories for three parties and independently confirmed 36 phase-safe and 54 cross-generation histories.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Exact counts match stdout and the stated finite model.

evidence: Re-derived no-early-advance induction, latch monotonicity, generation reset requirement, and registration/deregistration obligations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Successful advance requires complete current membership; failure uses a separate terminal transition.

evidence: Reviewed zero/one party, missing/duplicate/wrong-generation arrival, unequal loops, timeout, interruption, action failure, reset, stale token, registration race, deregistration, phase wrap, distributed misuse, and destruction.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: No private failure is allowed to strand fixed peers silently.

evidence: Checked arrival subset, complete-advance, exactly-once obligation, monotone latch, publication, atomic deregistration, group action outcome, epoch recovery, and quiescent lifecycle invariants.
invariant_checking.notes: Party accounting and application success remain separate.

evidence: Reviewed fixed-generation induction, cross-generation counterexample, early-exit deadlock, reset contamination, and distributed-boundary argument.
proof_review.notes: Safety, liveness, memory visibility, and scalability are not conflated.

evidence: Audited reusable-barrier schema, phase model, latch semantics, phaser membership, topology discussion, and safety-critical boundary.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The schema is explicitly non-executable and API claims remain version-scoped.

evidence: Reproduced one executable Python result and confirmed one schematic fence is intentionally skipped with a reason.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Evidence disclaims real threads, blocking, wakeups, memory ordering, failure, hierarchy, dynamic registration, and production implementation.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among latch, cyclic barrier, phaser, party, generation, arrival, wait, deregistration, breakage, reset, epoch, and termination.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed iterative algorithms, completion actions, deadlines, cancellation, structured failure, dynamic tasks, topology, observability, recovery, distributed limits, race tests, and shutdown.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives generation-indexed obligations from first principles through production recovery using ten distinct examples and five progressively demanding matched exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, aerospace, medical, clinical, controls, hardware, numerical, real-time, functional-safety, cybersecurity, certification, regulatory, or human-factors review is claimed. Finite enumeration and manual analysis do not prove a production barrier, timing, scalability, distributed coordination, or safety-critical deployment fitness.
